What happens to my Snapchat when I die?

By the Afterkeep research team · Reviewed on 19 Oct 2026

Short answer: Snapchat won't give anyone access to a deceased person's account, and its help page for people who have died describes no memorialisation option. Snapchat says it only accepts requests from a verified email address linked to the account. Deleting it needs a login at accounts.snapchat.com: the account is deactivated for 30 days, then permanently deleted after 30 more.

Key facts

  • No account access for anyone, including family
  • No memorialisation option described by Snapchat
  • Requests accepted only from the account's verified email
  • Deletion: 30 days deactivated, then permanently deleted after 30 more days

How do I prepare my Snapchat account?

  1. Save the Memories you want kept: log in at accounts.snapchat.com, open My Data, turn on 'Export your Memories', choose a date range and submit. Download the ZIP when Snapchat emails you.
  2. Keep the email address linked to your Snapchat account in a password manager with emergency access. Snapchat only accepts requests from that verified email.
  3. Write your username and your wishes (keep or delete) in your digital estate plan.
  4. After a death: Snapchat's documented route is Delete My Account at accounts.snapchat.com, which needs the login. Check with the executor before using someone else's login; otherwise contact Snapchat Support through its help site.

Read the official policy ↗

What documents do heirs need?

  • Access to the account's login, or to the verified email address linked to the account
  • Snapchat publishes no document list for deceased users. Have the death certificate and your ID ready in case Support asks

How long does it take?

Data exports: Snapchat aims to deliver within 7 days; large downloads take longer. Deletion: the account is deactivated for 30 days (it can be reactivated in that time) and permanently deleted after 30 more days. Data that isn't downloaded in the first 30 days is permanently deleted after 60 days.

What can't be recovered?

  • Anything inside the account that wasn't exported, because Snapchat doesn't grant account access
  • All account data after permanent deletion, apart from what Snapchat keeps for legal, security and business needs (such as purchase records)

Frequently asked questions

What happens to my Snapchat when I die?

Snapchat won't give anyone access to a deceased person's account, and its help page for people who have died describes no memorialisation option. Snapchat says it only accepts requests from a verified email address linked to the account. Deleting it needs a login at accounts.snapchat.com: the account is deactivated for 30 days, then permanently deleted after 30 more.

Can family get into a dead person's Snapchat?

No. Snapchat says its privacy policies don't allow it to grant access to the account.

Does Snapchat memorialise accounts?

Snapchat's help page for a person who passed away doesn't describe a memorialisation option. It covers requesting data by authenticated people and deleting the account.

How do I save Snapchat Memories?

Log in at accounts.snapchat.com, open My Data, turn on 'Export your Memories', pick a date range and submit. Snapchat emails a link; unzip the file and open index.html to download your Memories.

How long until a deleted Snapchat account is gone?

It's deactivated for 30 days, when it can still be reactivated, then permanently deleted after 30 more days. Snapchat says the second period is 180 days in India.

Who can ask Snapchat to act on an account?

Snapchat says it only accepts requests from a verified email address associated with the account, so access to that email matters.
